summary: Jonathan tracks the carriers: Thomas Snelling is drunk, but his boss Joseph Smollet gives destinations from a dog-eared notebook: six boxes to 197 Chicksand Street, Mile End New Town, and six to Jamaica Lane, Bermondsey, plus a tip about Sam Bloxam. Next day Jonathan decodes a phonetically spelled address, chases Bloxam through Walworth and Poplar to a cold storage building at Cross Angel Street, and learns nine boxes were carried to an empty house in Piccadilly by an old man with a white moustache of unnatural strength. He finds the house, learns from grooms and then Mitchell, Sons & Candy that the buyer is Count de Ville, who paid cash. Seward studies Renfield's talk of souls and life and deduces that the Count has visited him. The party plans to sterilise all earth between sunrise and sunset and prepares horses. Renfield is found lying in blood after a yell.

scenes.title: Snelling and Smollet
scenes.summary: Snelling is drunk. Smollet checks his notebook: six boxes to 197 Chicksand Street, Mile End New Town, six to Jamaica Lane, Bermondsey. Hint of a further job by Sam Bloxam at Purfleet.
scenes.key_quote: there were, he said, six in the cartload which he took from Carfax and left at 197, Chicksand Street, Mile End New Town

scenes.title: Phonetic address hunt
scenes.summary: The scrap reads 'Sam Bloxam, Korkrans, 4, Poters Cort, Bartel Street, Walworth. Arsk for the depite.' Jonathan decodes the misspellings and tips the deputy.
scenes.key_quote: phonetic spelling had again misled me

scenes.title: Finding Bloxam at Poplar
scenes.location: Cross Angel Street cold storage building
scenes.summary: Bloxam says he made two trips from Carfax to Piccadilly with nine boxes, helped by a strong thin old man with a white moustache who needed no key.
scenes.key_quote: he was the strongest chap I ever struck, an’ him a old feller, with a white moustache, one that thin you would think he couldn’t throw a shadder.

scenes.title: The Piccadilly house
scenes.location: Piccadilly, near the Junior Constitutional and mews behind
scenes.summary: Jonathan finds the dusty untenanted house with shutters up and a torn notice board; the grooms recall a 'For Sale' board from Mitchell, Sons & Candy.
scenes.key_quote: The windows were encrusted with dust, and the shutters were up.

scenes.title: The house agents
scenes.summary: The suave agent refuses to name the buyer until Jonathan says he acts for Lord Godalming.
scenes.key_quote: The affairs of their clients are absolutely safe in the hands of Mitchell, Sons, & Candy.

scenes.title: Council by the fire
scenes.summary: Party debates how to break into Piccadilly and reads aloud Jonathan's diary; plan to wait for the agent's letter.
scenes.key_quote: Say! how are we going to get into that house?

scenes.title: Renfield on souls and life
scenes.summary: Renfield disclaims wanting souls, stops at the word 'drink', fears the burden of souls; Seward deduces he expects a human life from the Count. Later Renfield sings and folds a scrap of paper into a notebook.
scenes.key_quote: Merciful God! the Count has been to him, and there is some new scheme of terror afoot!

scenes.title: Agency letter
scenes.summary: The letter gives No. 347 Piccadilly, former owner executors of Archibald Winter-Suffield, purchaser Count de Ville paying cash.
scenes.key_quote: The purchaser is a foreign nobleman, Count de Ville

scenes.title: Plan and Renfield's accident
scenes.summary: Horses are readied; Van Helsing researches ancient medicine at the British Museum. A wild yell from Renfield; he is found face down in blood.
scenes.key_quote: found him lying on his face on the floor, all covered with blood.

locations.quote: Mr. Joseph Smollet at home and in his shirtsleeves, taking a late tea out of a saucer.

locations.name: Cross Angel Street cold storage building
locations.description: New 'cold storage' warehouse under construction in Poplar with gatekeeper and foreman.

locations.name: No. 347 Piccadilly
locations.description: High stone-fronted house with a bow, high steps to the door, dusty windows and shutters, black framework, scaled paint, balcony with loose white-edged boards where a notice board was torn off; mews behind. Inside is a big empty hall.
locations.quote: It’s a ’igh ’un with a stone front with a bow on it, an’ ’igh steps up to the door.

locations.name: Renfield's room
locations.description: Room with observation trap, bed, stool in centre, scattered sugar and flies returning.
locations.quote: he had spread out his sugar as of old

locations.name: Seward's study fireside
locations.quote: all gathered round the fire in the study

creatures.quote: he took up ’is end o’ the boxes like they was pounds of tea

creatures.name: Renfield
creatures.description: Zoophagous madman linked to the Count.

vampire_lore.rule: Count can move earth boxes himself
vampire_lore.detail: He lifts them as if light and travels ahead of the carter.
vampire_lore.quote: the Count could, it was evident, handle the earth-boxes himself.

vampire_lore.detail: Boxes sent east, south and Piccadilly; plan likely covers all quarters.
vampire_lore.quote: The north and west were surely never meant to be left out of his diabolical scheme

vampire_lore.detail: Uses the name Count de Ville, pays in notes.
vampire_lore.quote: paying the purchase money in notes ‘over the counter,’

vampire_lore.rule: Sterilise earth between sunrise and sunset
vampire_lore.detail: Catch him at weakest without refuge.
vampire_lore.quote: We must sterilise all the imported earth between sunrise and sunset

vampire_lore.detail: His changes follow the Count's doings; the Count has promised him a higher life.
vampire_lore.quote: His moods have so followed the doings of the Count

vampire_lore.detail: The thin old man could 'hardly throw a shadder'.
vampire_lore.quote: you would think he couldn’t throw a shadder.

puzzles.name: Decode the phonetic address
puzzles.book_solution: Jonathan reads by sound: Potter's Court, Corcoran's, deputy.
puzzles.game_idea: Word puzzle where the player re-spells phonetic Cockney clues to find places and people.
puzzles.quote: Mr. Smollet’s spelling misled me, as I asked for Poter’s Court instead of Potter’s Court.

puzzles.name: Identify the house
puzzles.book_solution: Stone front with bow, high steps, near white church, beyond the Junior Constitutional; torn notice-board.
puzzles.game_idea: Street-scene matching puzzle with facade clues.
puzzles.quote: it was only a few doors from a big white church or somethink of the kind, not long built.

puzzles.name: Extract the buyer's name
puzzles.book_solution: Invokes Lord Godalming's name and address.
puzzles.game_idea: Social dialogue puzzle choosing credentials and tone.
puzzles.quote: These words put a different complexion on affairs.

puzzles.name: Get into Piccadilly
puzzles.book_solution: Unsolved here; hope for key from agency.
puzzles.game_idea: Stealth/legitimacy puzzle: obtain key legitimately or enter at night unseen.
puzzles.quote: It will be a mighty different thing to commit burglary in Piccadilly, either by day or night.

puzzles.name: Decipher Renfield's behaviour
puzzles.book_solution: Seward lists contradictions and deduces the Count visited.
puzzles.game_idea: Deduction board connecting statements to a conclusion.
puzzles.quote: Logically all these things point one way!
